sdfGenerator.title: Face Shadow SDF Generator
sdfGenerator.copy: `Face Shadow SDF Generator` is a desktop tool that loads `FBX` meshes and generates stylized shadow maps based on the current 3D view direction and UV layout. It can work with a single mesh, or with multiple meshes selected together when one UV target is split across several mesh pieces.

cards.title: Mesh-aware generation
cards.body: The result is generated from the actual mesh shape and the current 3D preview direction, not from a flat UV image alone.

cards.title: Manual correction included
cards.body: The workflow covers `UV Select`, manual brush correction, opposite-light rebake, and packed texture export in one place.

cards.title: Multi-mesh support
cards.body: If one face target is split across several meshes that share the same UV target, they can be handled together as one working selection.

meta.body: This tool is built for fast iteration on stylized face shadow maps, with manual cleanup available when the generated result needs additional control. Automatic generation, direct paint correction, and packed export live in the same workflow.

image.alt: Face Shadow SDF Generator English interface
image.caption: Main workspace view. The landscape layout keeps the 3D preview, UV work area, and result inspection connected in one flow.

sections.title: Key features
items: `FBX` loading through a Blender backend with mesh, normal, UV, and material data
`UV Map` selection when multiple UV layers exist
Shadow generation based on the current 3D preview direction
Manual correction with `Dark Shadow`, `Light Accent`, and `Erase Feature Paint`
Mirrored paint transfer through `Mirror Feature Paint`
Packed output in `rg.png` with `R = main` and `G = flipped`
Transparent outside-UV export and multilingual UI support

sections.title: Requirements
items: An `FBX` file that contains mesh and UV data
The Blender path can be assigned and saved inside the app

entries.title: `main.png`
entries.body: Primary generated result.

entries.title: `flipped.png`
entries.body: A rebaked result using the opposite lighting direction, not just a mirrored image.

entries.title: `rg.png`
entries.body: Packed output with `R = main` and `G = flipped`.

entries.title: `mask.png`
entries.body: Working and export mask.

entries.title: `asym.png`
entries.body: Derived output generated from `main` and `flipped`.

sections.title: Basic workflow
items: If the Blender path is not detected automatically, assign `blender.exe`.
Select the mesh or mesh group you want to work on.
Choose the UV option from `UV Map`.
Confirm the working direction in the 3D preview.
If needed, select UV islands in `UV Select`.
If needed, refine details with the manual brush.

sections.title: Recommended first pass
items: Generate one pass with the `Balanced` preset.
Reduce the working area with UV selection.
Only then add final detail with the brush.

entries.title: Left panel
entries.body: Handles the Blender path, `FBX` file selection, mesh list, `UV Map` selection, version label, and language selector.

entries.title: Center panel
entries.body: Shows the 3D preview, the UV selection / brush workspace, and the result preview.

entries.title: Right panel
entries.body: Contains UV selection settings, brush settings, UV display settings, presets, bake / output settings, layer settings, and output folder controls.

entries.title: `Mesh Selection`
entries.body:
`Mesh List` is the imported mesh list sorted A-Z by name.
Multiple meshes can be selected together when they represent one working target.
`UV Map` chooses the UV option used by the current mesh or selected mesh group.

entries.title: `UV Selection`
entries.body:
`Select All UV` selects every visible UV island, while `Clear UV Selection` clears the current selection.
When `Use selected UV islands` is enabled, generation only uses the selected islands.

entries.title: `Manual Feature Brush`
entries.body:
Includes `Select UV Islands`, `Place Dark Shadow`, `Place Light Accent`, and `Erase Feature Paint` modes.
`Brush size %` changes brush size, `Mirror Feature Paint` copies the paint to the opposite side, and `Clear Feature Paint` removes all manual paint.

entries.title: `Lighting Presets`
entries.body: `Balanced` is the default preset, `Defined` increases left-right contrast, `Dramatic` pushes stronger direction and contrast, and `Extreme` gives a very strong stylized result.

entries.title: `Bake / Output`
entries.body:
`Resolution` supports `512`, `1K`, `2K`, `4K`, `8K`, and `16K`.
You can adjust `Bake contrast`, `Bake ambient`, `Light X / Y / Z`, `Bake smoothing`, `UV edge padding`, `Feature strength`, and `Feature blur`.
`Transparent outside UV`, `Anime feature shadows`, `Use current 3D view`, and `Reset 3D View` also belong to this area.

entries.title: `Advanced Layers`
entries.body: `Layer count`, `Growth intensity`, `Horizontal growth`, `Vertical growth`, `Blend mode`, and `SDF radius` control the intermediate generation layers and the final blend behavior.

entries.title: 3D Preview
entries.body: Drag to rotate.

entries.title: UV Select
entries.body:
Mouse wheel zooms in and out, middle drag pans, left click selects UV, and `Ctrl + Left Click` adds or removes from the selection.
Left drag paints, right drag erases.

sections.title: Tips
items: It is usually more stable to inspect the generated result first and only then add brush corrections.
`flipped` is not a simple image flip, so it can still be useful on asymmetrical UV layouts.
If you want matching detail on both sides, `Mirror Feature Paint` is the faster option.
For multi-mesh work, first confirm that the selected meshes share the same `UV Map` target.
Generate only the final result at very high resolution; use `2K` or `4K` while iterating.

entries.title: Nothing generates after mesh selection
entries.body: Check whether the selected meshes share a common UV option.

entries.title: Dark seams appear on UV borders
entries.body:
Try lowering `UV edge padding` further into negative values.
You can also raise `Bake smoothing` slightly.

entries.title: The result feels too weak
entries.body:
Try the `Defined`, `Dramatic`, or `Extreme` presets.
Raise `Bake contrast` and `Feature strength`.

entries.title: The result feels too strong
entries.body: Lower `Bake contrast` and raise `Bake ambient`.

entries.title: The workflow feels slow
entries.body: Work at a lower resolution first and only switch to a high-resolution export at the end.
